summary: Intermittent 429s on multipart callback flow due to signed-URL multipath + liveness probes draining dedicated burst pool
description: Issue summary: Customer DataWave reports periodic 429s during a multipart callback / signed-URL confirmation flow. The failures occur intermittently and coincide with bulk callback waves and a scheduled internal health-check job. Impact: production callback failures (webhook success rate drops ~12% during waves), delayed ingest processing, customer-visible errors and alerting. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (prod-us-west) with priority lanes configured for low-latency stream traffic; callbacks handled through signed URLs served by edge-proxy; healthcheck/liveness probes originating from their orchestrator are visible in telemetry.
impact: Approx 12% of callback attempts rejected with 429 during high-concurrency callback waves. Customer sees delayed processing of multi-part uploads and retries leading to duplicate callbacks and billing noise. Alerts triggered in their SRE slack channel #dw-sre and Redwood support #support.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure multipart upload with signed-callback URLs using our edge-proxy. 2) Simulate 200 concurrent callback confirmations from a distributed worker pool. 3) Ensure customer orchestrator health-checks (1s interval) run in parallel. 4) Observe 429 responses from Redwood endpoint on ~10-15% of callbacks during the spike.
observed_behavior: Callbacks intermittently receive 429 with rate-limit headers indicating token window exhaustion. Telemetry shows many small requests (callbacks + health probes) counted against the same burst pool and priority lane refill, consuming burst credits quickly and producing sawtooth 429 waves.
expected_behavior: Signed-URL callbacks should be accounted using the configured route/priority lane isolation. Health-check probes should not consume the same burst credits as application callbacks, and dedicated burst pools should avoid contention between low-latency lanes and background liveness traffic.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:02:11Z - INFO - edge-proxy rewrite host header from dw-callbacks -> signed.edge.redwood
2026-03-10T15:02:11Z - DEBUG - refill-window: 60s - burst-pool-id: dedicated-pool-42 - priority-lane: low-latency
customer_notes: We started seeing spikes after increasing worker parallelism from 50 -> 200 and enabling a short-lived readiness probe in our job manager. We haven't changed our SDK. We see many callbacks succeed but a noisy minority fail with 429s and then succeed after retries. This is causing duplicate processing downstream.
comments: Alex Kim (Support): Thanks for the report — collecting initial traces and rate-limiter metrics from the dedicated pool. Can you confirm whether callbacks reuse the same API key or multiple ephemeral keys?
DW SRE (Customer): Callbacks use a single service API key per cluster. Health-checks originate from a separate internal service that hits a lightweight /status route using the same key.

Priya Shah (Eng): Observed correlation between health-check timestamps and 429 pulses. Edge-proxy Host header rewrite is causing signed-url path to be treated as a new fingerprint in some ingress paths — possible duplicate accounting across routes. Adding @edge-team for investigation.

Edge Team (comment): We see host rewrite for signed URLs due to legacy transform; proposing a short-term config to normalize host header. Also found that internal health probes are not excluded from tenant burst accounting on dedicated pools by default.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Health-checks + callbacks are sharing the same burst/bandwidth bucket due to route fingerprint overlap, exhausting burst credits during high concurrency.

Hypothesis B: Edge-proxy rewrites (Host header) cause signed-url requests to be tagged as separate route fingerprints which interact poorly with priority-lane isolation logic, leading to double-counting across two refill windows.

Telemetry: Burst pool 'dedicated-pool-42' shows repeated small windows where refill credits are drained within 3-8s during callback waves. Priority-lane meter shows borrow events into low-latency lane from background pool.

Correlated events: Customer's orchestrator readiness job runs every 1s; each probe issues a lightweight GET to /status that was being counted against the tenant token bucket (we should ideally exempt internal health probes or route them to the background bucket).

Edge trace: We identified mismatched fingerprinting for signed-url paths when Host header != expected value; when mismatch occurs, the edge creates a distinct route hash and both hashes draw from adjacent token windows in some rate-limiter versions (edge-rlv v2.3.1).
short_term_workarounds: 1) Ask customer to temporarily increase burst allowances on their dedicated pool (provision + add burst credits) to eliminate immediate 429s during reconfiguration.
2) Patch orchestrator to route liveness/health-check probes to a non-counting path or a background-only route that uses a separate burst pool.
3) Recommend SDK update to include an 'x-client-purpose: health' header so we can filter out probes server-side until permanent fix.
4) Edge team: enable host-normalization feature-flag on the customer's edge-proxy to avoid route fingerprint duplication (rollbackable).
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Edge: Deploy PR to normalize host header and improve route fingerprinting to avoid duplicate accounting (see PR #4321). 2) Rate limiter: adjust refill logic so that route-hash collisions do not cause cross-window double-debiting; add dedupe to token accounting. 3) Console/Docs: add guidance and a 'healthcheck-exempt' configuration and an example for orchestrators. 4) Customer: adopt separated route for liveness or use distinct service key for probes to guarantee isolation.
resolution: Mitigations applied: host-normalization feature flag enabled for the customer's edge-proxy on 2026-03-12 UTC resulting in immediate reduction of dual-fingerprint events. Customer set health-checks to a 'probe' header and we configured server-side filter to route probe traffic into background burst pool. After changes, callback 429s dropped from 12% -> 0.8% in next 24h. Planned: ship rate-limiter dedupe fix in v2.4.0 (tracked in internal INT-4490).
postmortem_followups: Create a small runbook entry for Dedicated customers describing how to isolate liveness probes: runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.company/runbooks/dedicated-liveness-isolation
Add a telemetry alert to detect 'route-hash divergence' where identical signed-url paths generate multiple route fingerprints.
Ship rate-limiter fix in v2.4.0 and coordinate a minor rollout to avoid refill-window regressions.
resolution_status: Partial fix deployed; customer agreed to permanent scheduled release for rate-limiter dedupe in next patch. Monitoring in place.
